home.badge: NCBI RefSeq · Primer3 · Every step traceable
home.tagline: Enter a gene. Review traceable primer candidates.
home.page_sub: A RefSeq transcript is selected by stated rules and candidates are generated with Primer3. When reference data are available, paired amplification is screened against a fixed genome and its matched RefSeq RNA collection. Templates, parameters, reference versions, and decision boundaries remain reviewable.
home.how_sub: Define the target. The pipeline handles the rest.
home.how_step1_desc: Enter a gene name or paste a DNA sequence.
home.how_step2_desc: Select a RefSeq transcript, generate candidates with Primer3, and run the available paired-amplification screen.
home.how_step3_desc: Review sequences, amplicons, scores, and screening results, then export the record.
home.primer_card_desc: Generate qPCR candidates from a gene, with transcript, exon-span, and scoring evidence.
home.pcr_card_desc: Design standard, colony, or high-fidelity PCR primers from a DNA template.
home.grna_card_desc: Scan PAM sites and rank gRNAs by predicted activity.
home.blast_card_desc: Submit an NCBI BLAST query and inspect hits and alignments.
home.features_subtitle: Key parameters and screening results stay with the sequence.
home.feat_transcript_desc: Shows the RefSeq accession and selection rule.
home.feat_exon_desc: Labels exon-spanning designs or intron distance and flags the need for a no-RT control.
home.feat_blast_desc: Reports target products, same-gene isoforms, and other-gene products separately; incomplete evidence cannot pass.
home.feat_score_desc: Shows Tm, GC%, hairpin, self-complementarity, dimer risk, and component scores.
home.feat_props_desc: Self-complementarity Tm, 3′-end Tm, hairpin Tm, GC clamp — the raw numbers, not a summary.
home.feat_export_desc: Export a CSV table and an HTML report with method notes for laboratory records, comparison, and review.
home.meta_desc: Enter a gene name, select a RefSeq transcript by stated rules, generate candidates with Primer3, and review traceable paired-amplification specificity evidence.

primer.title: qPCR Primer Design
primer.subtitle: Generate qPCR primer candidates from a gene or DNA sequence, with paired genome and transcript evidence when versioned local references are available
primer.blast_hits_scope_note: These hits come from the NCBI RefSeq RNA transcript collection. They help screen transcript-level off-target risk, but they are not equivalent to genome-wide PCR specificity validation.
primer.blast_error: RefSeq RNA BLAST is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.
primer.blast_no_hits: No hit was found for this primer in the RefSeq RNA transcript collection.
primer.blast_target_found: Target transcript {accession} was found in the returned set
primer.blast_target_missing: Target transcript {accession} was not found in the returned set
primer.blast_target_unspecified: No target accession is available for this custom sequence, so transcript specificity cannot pass
primer.blast_hit_limit_warning: The BLAST return limit was reached; additional hits may be hidden
primer.loading_msg: Querying NCBI, designing primers, and screening specificity...
primer.wait_body: Usually completes in 30–90 seconds. If NCBI is under load, it may take up to 3 minutes. If the external service does not respond, the workflow degrades gracefully or prompts you to retry.
primer.empty_subtitle: Enter a gene name to select a reference transcript, design primer candidates, and run the available specificity screen.
primer.candidate_section_intro: Compare sequences, amplicon length, and key quality metrics first. Expand a candidate for score components, specificity evidence, and structure parameters.
primer.sequence_direction_note: Both forward (F) and reverse (R) primers are shown 5′→3′. The reverse primer is the reverse complement of its binding site and can be ordered exactly as shown.
primer.known_section_intro: These sequences come from reviewable database, publication, or vendor records and are ordered by transcript match and evidence type. Evidence codes describe the source; they are not confidence scores. A source record and PrimerCat's current-reference check remain distinct claims.
primer.known_empty: No ready-made pair was found in the current reviewable source catalog. The PrimerCat candidates above were still computed for this gene; no source record does not mean the gene cannot be designed.
primer.known_catalog_scope: Current species catalog: {genes} gene records · {pairs} sourced pairs · updated {date}
primer.known_catalog_scope_note: The gene count is the searchable NCBI Gene index, not a claim that every gene has a ready-made or experimentally validated pair. Only records with a retained original source are included.
primer.known_evidence_vendor_tested_note: The vendor reports satisfactory qPCR data under its stated instrument and cycling program; this is not independent peer-reviewed validation.
primer.known_evidence_experimental_record_note: The source links amplification, dissociation, gel, sequencing, or related experimental records. Fitness still depends on the sample, reagents, and assay conditions.
primer.known_evidence_database_record_note: The sequence and parameters are traceable to a database record, but this entry is not marked as having a complete public experimental-validation record.
primer.known_evidence_published_record_note: The sequence is traceable to a publication; the original sample, reagents, and cycling conditions still need to be reviewed separately.
primer.known_evidence_computed_database_note: This pair comes from computational design in an external database and is not equivalent to wet-lab validation.
primer.known_transcript_exact_accession_note: Source target {source} and current template {target} have the same accession and version.
primer.known_transcript_accession_root_note: Source target {source} and current template {target} share an accession, but the same version is not pinned on both sides. A RefSeq version change denotes a sequence update, so the amplicon location still needs review.
primer.known_transcript_different_transcript_no: Source target {source} is not the current template {target}. This is a same-gene reference, not a direct match for the selected isoform.
primer.known_transcript_not_assessed_note: No target transcript was available for comparison, so the match to source target {source} has not been assessed.
primer.known_check_checking_note: Running paired-amplification checks against the fixed genome and RefSeq RNA references for the currently selected transcript.
primer.known_check_passed_note: The joint paired screen on {assembly} found no cross-gene product for {transcript}; the observed target product is {product}. This remains computational evidence.
primer.known_check_review_note: This pair did not satisfy every conservative rule for {transcript} on {assembly}; the target product is {product}. Review the original source and assay conditions before use.
primer.known_check_partial_note: Only part of the local reference set was available for {transcript} ({assembly}); the target product is {product}, so full specificity cannot be inferred.
primer.known_check_unavailable_note: A versioned-reference check could not be run for {transcript}; the target product is {product}. The source remains available, but this pair has not been validated by PrimerCat.
primer.known_disclaimer: Sourced records are provided for comparison and traceability, not as an ordering recommendation. Confirm the intended isoform, sample variants, efficiency, a single melt peak, and negative controls before formal use.
primer.evidence_section_intro: Reference transcript, Primer3 constraints, screening funnel, specificity scope, and transcript structure.
primer.design_basis_intro: These values are from the actual design and screening run — use them to verify where each primer pair came from.
primer.basis_scoring_caption: Ranking combines Tm, GC%, completed specificity evidence, exon-spanning behavior, and dimer risk, then returns pairs from highest to lowest score.
primer.basis_scope_joint_pair: Versioned reference genome + RefSeq RNA · paired-amplicon simulation
primer.basis_scope_note_body: A positive BLAST score here only means the primer pair shows no obvious non-target hits within the RefSeq RNA transcript collection. That improves transcript-level confidence, but it is not the same as genome-wide PCR specificity validation. Experimental use should still be backed by genome-level in-silico checks or wet-lab validation.
primer.basis_genome_note_title: How to read the paired-genome screen
primer.basis_genome_note_body: Pass means the two primers form exactly one 50–5000 bp product inside the target transcript's annotated locus on the versioned reference genome, with no result truncation. It does not assess sample variants, transcript isoforms, amplification efficiency, or wet-lab product purity.
primer.basis_joint_note_title: How to read the joint screen
primer.basis_joint_note_body: Paired amplification is simulated separately on the fixed reference genome and its matched RefSeq RNA collection. A joint pass requires an amplifiable target transcript, no product assigned to another gene or an unclassified transcript, and either one target-locus genomic product or no contiguous genomic product. Same-gene isoforms are reported separately. This remains computational evidence, not experimental validation.
primer.reason_subtitle: This pair is currently ranked #{rank}. Here is how it performs across the five key dimensions.
primer.reason_no_cautions: No prominent risk item was found within the current thresholds. This candidate ranks well because its metrics are balanced; experimental validation is still required.
primer.reason_tm_ideal: Both primers sit in the ideal Tm window and the pair is tightly matched.
primer.reason_tm_ok: Tm remains usable, but the pair is not as tightly matched as the best candidates.
primer.reason_tm_watch: Tm drifts from the ideal window or the pair mismatch is large enough to reduce amplification consistency.
primer.reason_gc_ideal: GC% is in the ideal band, giving a more balanced annealing profile.
primer.reason_gc_ok: GC% is still acceptable, but not in the best-performing range.
primer.reason_gc_watch: GC% is too high or too low, which can hurt annealing efficiency and specificity.
primer.reason_specificity_validated: The available specificity screen found no evident non-target amplification.
primer.reason_specificity_partial: Specificity evidence is incomplete, so it only counts as partial support.
primer.reason_specificity_unvalidated: Specificity screening was incomplete, so this dimension cannot be treated as passed.
primer.reason_genome_specificity_validated: Exactly one target-locus amplicon and no additional paired genomic product were found.
primer.reason_genome_specificity_offtarget: The paired-genome screen found an extra product, could not anchor the target, or was truncated, so no pass is assigned.
primer.check_genome_pair_specific: One target product; no additional paired product
primer.check_genome_pair_no_product: No classifiable target genomic amplicon was formed
primer.check_genome_pair_unanchored: The target transcript could not be uniquely anchored to the genome annotation
primer.check_genome_pair_truncated: The hit return limit was reached; no pass can be assigned
primer.check_genome_pair_offtarget: An additional or ambiguous paired amplicon was found
primer.genome_pair_scope_note: Each primer is aligned to the versioned reference genome, then candidate amplicons are formed by contig, opposing orientation, and product length. The intended product is anchored with the RefSeq GTF transcript locus.
primer.genome_pair_no_products: No paired amplicon is available to display.
primer.check_transcriptome_gene_specific: Target transcript amplifiable; no other-gene product found
primer.check_transcriptome_isoform_specific: Only the selected transcript product was found
primer.check_transcriptome_same_gene_isoform: Other isoforms of the same gene are also amplifiable
primer.check_transcriptome_cross_gene: Another-gene or unclassified transcript product was found
primer.check_transcriptome_target_missing: The selected transcript product was not confirmed in the fixed annotation
primer.check_transcriptome_truncated: The transcript hit limit was reached; no pass can be assigned
primer.check_genome_no_contiguous_product: No contiguous genomic product; the target product is confirmed by the transcript screen
primer.transcriptome_pair_scope_note: Each primer is aligned to the version-pinned accessioned RefSeq RNA collection paired with the reference assembly, then candidate products are formed by transcript, opposing orientation, and product length.
primer.transcriptome_isoform_yes: Only the selected isoform was found in the fixed annotation
primer.transcriptome_isoform_no: Other same-gene isoforms can also be amplified
primer.transcriptome_no_products: No transcript amplicon is available to display.
primer.reason_specificity_offtarget: The available specificity screen suggests potential non-target amplification, so this dimension was penalized.
primer.reason_exon_yes: The pair spans {n} exon junction(s), which helps suppress genomic DNA interference.
primer.reason_exon_no: The pair does not span an exon junction, so it is less convincing for mRNA-focused qPCR use.
primer.reason_dimer_low: 3' self-complementarity and hairpin risk are both low, so dimer risk is limited.
primer.reason_dimer_ok: Structural risk is still below threshold, but not as clean as the strongest pairs.
primer.reason_dimer_watch: 3' self-complementarity or hairpin risk is elevated enough to potentially reduce amplification efficiency.
primer.check_blast_specific: No obvious non-target hit in RefSeq RNA
primer.check_blast_offtarget: Potential non-target hit in RefSeq RNA
primer.check_blast_unavailable: No transcript hit returned — insufficient evidence, review manually
primer.seq_placeholder: Paste target DNA sequence (200–3000 bp recommended)
primer.stopped_notice: Design stopped. You can adjust parameters and retry.
primer.stream_unavailable: The design service did not return a readable event stream.
primer.stream_incomplete: The design stream ended unexpectedly. Please retry.
primer.timeout_error: Request timed out (>3 min). NCBI servers are slow, please retry later.
primer.validate_gene_format: Gene name may only contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
primer.validate_seq_empty: Please paste a target DNA sequence.
primer.validate_seq_short: Sequence too short — 200 bp or more is recommended for primer design.
primer.validate_seq_invalid: Sequence contains invalid characters. Please use only A, T, G, C, N.
primer.progress_detail_fetch: Retrieving transcript and gene records from NCBI…
primer.progress_detail_custom_sequence: Using the submitted sequence as the design template.
primer.progress_detail_design: Generating candidate primer pairs with Primer3…
primer.progress_detail_candidates_ready: Candidate pairs are ready for specificity screening.
primer.progress_detail_screening: Screening candidate primers for specificity; this may take a moment…
primer.progress_detail_screening_timeout: Specificity screening did not finish within the time limit. Candidates will be returned with incomplete evidence.
primer.progress_detail_rank: Calculating scores and ordering candidate pairs…
primer.progress_detail_complete: Design complete. Candidate pairs are ready for review.
primer.result_summary: Returned {count} primer pairs ({specific} passed {screening} specificity screening; {exon} span exon junctions).
primer.result_summary_incomplete: Returned {count} primer pairs. Specificity screening was incomplete; {exon} pairs span exon junctions. Review the evidence record for each pair before use.
primer.blast_warning_body: {count} primer pair(s) did not complete screening or reached the return limit. Review the evidence before experimental use; an unknown state is not a pass.
primer.click_hint: Click any row to expand · Switch tabs for details
primer.data_realtime_note: — Real-time query, results reflect database state at query time
primer.help_intro: From a gene name to primer candidates with screening evidence, the system completes five steps automatically.
primer.help_data_body: NCBI RefSeq (transcripts and annotation) · versioned reference genome and matched RefSeq RNA when configured · Primer3 (primer design algorithm)
primer.help_output_body: Up to 5 candidate primer pairs with Tm, GC%, exon-spanning status, available specificity evidence, and composite score (0–100)
primer.help_step_query_title: Enter a gene name or custom sequence
primer.help_step_query_body: Two modes: ① Enter a gene symbol (e.g. TP53, Actb) and the system queries NCBI automatically; ② Paste a DNA sequence directly (200–3000 bp recommended).
primer.help_step_transcript_title: Select a reference transcript by rule
primer.help_step_transcript_body: Queries NCBI RefSeq in real time, filters NM_ protein-coding transcripts, and selects a design template using CDS completeness, exon count, and related rules.
primer.help_step_primer3_body: Runs Primer3 on the mRNA sequence to generate up to 30 candidate pairs and retain the first 10 by penalty score. Target ranges are Tm 58–62°C, GC% 40–60%, and product size 80–200 bp.
primer.help_step_specificity_body: When versioned reference data are configured, both primers are aligned separately to the reference genome and its matched RefSeq RNA collection, then candidate amplicons are formed by orientation and product length. Target transcripts, same-gene isoforms, other genes, and unclassified products are reported separately; a hit cap or incomplete evidence cannot pass. Other cases use the available backend stated on the result page.
primer.help_step_scoring_body: Primers are ranked by a weighted composite score (max 100) across five dimensions: Tm match, GC% balance, completed specificity evidence, exon-spanning design, and 3′-end self-complementarity.
primer.help_score_tm: Tm match (20 pts): both primers 58–62°C, difference < 2°C
primer.help_score_gc: GC% balance (20 pts): both primers 40–60% GC
primer.help_score_specificity: Specificity evidence (30 pts): awarded only when the active backend's complete decision rule passes. The fixed mouse joint screen additionally requires an amplifiable target transcript, no other-gene product, and a compatible target-locus genome result. This score is not experimental validation
primer.help_score_exon: Exon-spanning (20 pts): primers cross an exon junction or intron, reducing genomic-DNA interference risk
primer.help_score_dimer: 3′-end dimer (10 pts): self-complementarity Tm < 35°C, hairpin Tm < 24°C
primer.help_note_body: Mature mRNA lacks introns while genomic DNA retains them. A primer across an exon junction, or a pair spanning a sufficiently large intron, can reduce genomic-DNA interference. Performance depends on primer placement, intron length, and assay conditions; RT-qPCR should still include a no-RT control and experimental validation.

grna.title: CRISPR Guide Design
grna.subtitle: Scan PAM sites and rank gRNA candidates by predicted activity and off-target evidence.
grna.hero_meta_body: PAM scanning, activity ranking, and off-target screening
grna.gene_placeholder: e.g. TP53 — sequence fetched automatically from RefSeq
grna.locus_help: Optional. When provided, PrimerCat checks whether top-ranked guides match the specified locus.
grna.seq_placeholder: Paste the target region (200–1000 bp recommended)
grna.error_invalid_target_locus: Locus format should look like chr17:43044295-43044318 or chr17:43044295-43044318 (+).
grna.risk_note_body: Use rankings to shortlist candidates; validate editing efficiency and off-target risk experimentally.
grna.empty_subtitle: Enter a gene or target sequence to see guides, PAMs, cut positions, and screening evidence.
grna.readiness_loading_body: Checking what off-target screening is available for the selected species...
grna.readiness_template_body: Copy this into backend/.env and replace the example paths with your local genome files, then restart the backend.
grna.readiness_copy_failed: Copy failed — please select and copy manually.
grna.readiness_step_install: 1. Install bowtie2 and make sure it is on your PATH.
grna.readiness_step_index: 2. Build or download a Bowtie2 index for your species.
grna.readiness_step_env: 3. Fill in the paths above and restart the backend.
grna.readiness_action_ready: Genome-level off-target screening is active for this species.
grna.readiness_action_fallback: Basic NCBI BLAST off-target screening will be used. For higher-confidence results, configure a local genome index.
grna.readiness_action_disabled: Off-target screening is turned off in the current configuration.
grna.readiness_action_unavailable: Off-target screening is not available right now.
grna.readiness_action_bowtie: Install bowtie2 or update GRNA_BOWTIE2_PATH to a valid executable.
grna.readiness_action_env: Set {indexVar} and {fastaVar} to your local Bowtie2 index and reference FASTA.
grna.readiness_action_anchor: Locus checking requires genome-level screening to be configured first.
grna.readiness_anchor_note: Locus checking is enabled, but requires a local genome index to work.
grna.scope_hint: Full genome screening when available, BLAST otherwise
grna.error_short_sequence: Please enter a gene name or a DNA sequence of at least 23 bp.
grna.feature_activity_title: Guides ranked by predicted cutting efficiency
grna.feature_activity_body: SpCas9/SpCas9-NG and Cas12a use separate scoring models. Results are ranked so the most promising candidates appear first — a useful shortlist, not a guaranteed outcome.
grna.feature_offtarget_title: Every guide screened for off-target risk
grna.feature_offtarget_body: Each guide shows a clear screening status. When a local genome index is configured, screening runs genome-wide. Otherwise a BLAST-based screen is run and labeled as such.
grna.feature_evidence_title: Inspect every hit behind the ranking
grna.feature_evidence_body: Expand any candidate to inspect the guide+PAM sequence, highest-identity non-target match, and major genomic hits for candidate comparison.
grna.results_intro: Found {count} {cas} guide candidates. Off-target screening used {species}-filtered NCBI records.
grna.results_intro_genome: Found {count} {cas} guide candidates. Screened against the {species} reference genome.
grna.results_intro_fallback: Found {count} {cas} guide candidates. Full genome screening was unavailable — BLAST-based screening was used instead.
grna.fallback_body: A local genome index was not available for this run. Results are still useful as a first-pass screen, but this should not be treated as a complete genome-wide off-target analysis.
grna.activity_model_body: Scores are based on sequence features that correlate with cutting efficiency. They rank candidates usefully but are not an experimental success rate — always validate your top picks in the lab.
grna.offtarget_model_body: When a genome index is configured, guides are screened against the full species genome. Otherwise, NCBI BLAST is used as a fallback and the result is clearly labeled.
grna.scope_body: Genome index screening is more sensitive and covers the full genome. BLAST fallback is a useful first screen but is not equivalent to a dedicated genome-wide off-target analysis.
grna.offtarget_summary_clean: Only one confident genomic hit detected — consistent with the intended target.
grna.offtarget_summary_hits: {count} additional genomic hit(s) detected — review before use.
grna.offtarget_summary_anchor_missing: This guide did not hit the target locus you specified.
grna.offtarget_summary_no_hits: No confident genomic hit found — supporting evidence is limited.
grna.offtarget_summary_error: Off-target screening failed for this guide — do not treat it as validated.
grna.offtarget_summary_skipped: Off-target screening is not available for the selected species.
grna.activity_score_warning: Activity scores are sequence-feature predictions, not experimental measurements. Confirm candidates experimentally.
grna.activity_panel_body: Off-target risk also affects the final ranking, so a high activity score does not automatically mean rank #1.
grna.hit_annotation_ready_body: Hits below have been annotated with nearby gene and transcript information.
grna.hit_annotation_missing_body: Genomic hits found, but no gene annotation file is configured — gene and exon labels are not available.
grna.hit_annotation_fallback_body: No genome-coordinate hits in this run, so gene context labels are not available.
grna.hit_annotation_unavailable_inline: No gene annotation available for this hit.
grna.scope_note: Hits come from genome-level screening when the index is configured, or from BLAST when it is not. BLAST-based results are a useful screen but not equivalent to a full genome-wide off-target analysis.

pcr.title: Endpoint PCR Primer Design
pcr.subtitle: Design endpoint, colony, and high-fidelity PCR primers from DNA or FASTA templates with full amplicon and structure metrics.
pcr.hero_meta_body: Candidate sequences, amplicons, and structure metrics
pcr.preset_hint: Presets tune design parameters; the polymerase manual still takes priority
pcr.template_hint: Plain DNA or one FASTA record
pcr.sequence_placeholder:
>target
Paste at least 50 bp of DNA using A / C / G / T / N
pcr.target_toggle: Require the amplicon to cover a target region
pcr.target_toggle_hint: For a mutation, insert, or diagnostic region; coordinates are 1-based
pcr.design_boundary: This release performs Primer3 design, structure checks, and an optional screen of NCBI RefSeq genomic records. A limited remote screen is not complete reference-genome validation.
pcr.empty_body: Paste a template to see candidate sequences, amplicon positions, and quality metrics.
pcr.loading_body: Searching for candidates that satisfy product length, Tm, GC%, and structure constraints.
pcr.sequence_direction_note: Both forward (F) and reverse (R) primers are shown 5′→3′. The reverse primer is the reverse complement of its binding site and can be ordered exactly as shown.
pcr.specificity_title: Screen each pair against RefSeq genomic records
pcr.specificity_body: Choose a species, then screen any pair against RefSeq genomic records within NCBI nt. The screen looks for opposing hits 50–5000 bp apart. Remote result limits apply, so this is not complete reference-genome validation.
pcr.specificity_result_single_body: Only one returned RefSeq genomic record formed a candidate product. This still does not establish uniqueness across the complete reference genome.
pcr.specificity_result_multiple_body: This is a database-record count, not a count of independent off-target loci. Assembly or region records may represent the same biological locus; inspect their titles and product sizes and use a more complete genome validation when needed.
pcr.specificity_result_none: No paired genomic record in the returned results
pcr.specificity_result_none_body: The returned RefSeq genomic hits did not form a 50–5000 bp product. This does not prove that non-target amplification is absent.
pcr.specificity_result_unavailable_body: The remote query did not produce an interpretable result. Retry later; this pair must not be treated as validated.
pcr.specificity_scope_note: The screen is limited to RefSeq genomic records for this species within NCBI nt. Up to the first {limit} returned hits per primer are analysed for 50–5000 bp products, requiring an exact match at the final three 3′ bases. Different records may represent the same locus, so record counts are not independent off-target counts.
pcr.specificity_truncated_note: At least one primer reached the hit limit, so additional candidates may exist.
pcr.specificity_error_ncbi: NCBI BLAST is temporarily unavailable or the request timed out. Please retry later.
pcr.gradient_note: The annealing temperature is estimated from the lower primer Tm as a starting gradient only. Follow the selected polymerase instructions and optimise experimentally.
pcr.error_multiple_fasta: Only one FASTA record can be designed at a time.
pcr.error_empty: Paste a DNA or FASTA sequence.
pcr.error_invalid_chars: The sequence contains invalid characters. Use A, C, G, T, N, and whitespace only.
pcr.error_short: The template must contain at least 50 bp.
pcr.error_many_n: More than 10% of the template is ambiguous (N), so primers cannot be designed reliably.
pcr.error_product_range: The minimum product length must be smaller than the maximum.
pcr.error_tm_range: Tm values must satisfy minimum ≤ optimal ≤ maximum.
pcr.error_gc_range: Minimum GC% must be smaller than maximum GC%.
pcr.error_target_incomplete: Enter both the target start and target end.
pcr.error_target_range: The target coordinates are invalid or outside the template.
pcr.error_template_range: The template is shorter than the selected minimum product size.
pcr.error_primer3: Primer3 could not complete this design. Adjust the parameters and retry.
pcr.error_no_primers: No suitable pair was found. Try a wider product, Tm, or GC% range.
pcr.error_generic: Design failed. Check the input and try again.

tools.title: Research utilities
tools.intro: qPCR primers, CRISPR guides, NCBI BLAST, and routine lab calculations — every tool that is currently available is collected here.
tools.note: Each calculation states its data source, screening scope, and experimental-validation boundary.
tools.heroAsideBody: This page lists working tools only, with no placeholder destinations.
tools.heroMetricBody: Four core sequence tools plus three lab-bench tools.
whyItems: Results distinguish algorithmic predictions, database screening, and experimental validation.
Chinese and English interfaces use the same parameters, scoring logic, and result structure.
Only real, reachable tools are listed; planned features are never presented as live.
tools.card_primer_body: Generate candidates from a gene name or DNA sequence with exon-spanning checks, reviewable specificity evidence, and transparent scoring.
tools.card_pcr_body: Design standard, colony, and high-fidelity PCR primers from DNA or FASTA with amplicons, coordinates, structure checks, and order-sheet export.
tools.card_grna_body: Scan PAM sites on both strands, rank candidates, and run genome or BLAST off-target screening according to backend availability.
tools.card_blast_body: Run blastn, blastp, blastx, or tblastn and inspect ranked hits, identity, E-value, and alignment details.
tools.card_mw_body: Parse chemical formulas, calculate molar mass and elemental composition, prepare solutions, and compute dilutions — all in one place.
tools.card_solutions_body: Calculate molar solutions, stock dilutions, and percentages, then scale sourced PBS, TAE, TBE, Tris-HCl, and SDS recipes to target volume.
tools.card_safety_body: Search common reagents by name, CAS, or formula for hazard summaries, representative H-codes, handling controls, incompatibilities, and original sources.
